rationale: Tests accurate recall of BNS 2023 Section 63 replacing IPC Section 375 — a frequently confused statutory update that has direct implications for medicolegal report formatting.
Tests understanding of POCSO's age threshold and its gender-neutral application — commonly confused as applying only to females.
Addresses the duty to examine without preconditions — a medicolegal obligation frequently misunderstood by clinicians who wait for police referral.
Tests the specific procedural requirement for the examination of the accused — a distinct examination governed by BNSS Section 397.

Tests knowledge of the Navtej Singh Johar landmark ruling — the constitutional basis for decriminalisation of consensual same-sex conduct, which clinicians must understand to avoid discriminatory practice.
Evaluates the clinician's understanding that absence of physical injury does not negate a legal finding of rape — a critical principle for fair medico-legal reporting.
Tests the DSM-5/ICD-11 paraphilia versus paraphilic disorder distinction — the most clinically and legally important conceptual boundary in this domain.
Applies classification of paraphilic disorders to a clinical scenario — identifying exhibitionistic disorder as the correct diagnosis prevents misclassification in forensic reports.
Evaluates understanding of the scientific invalidity of hymen-based virginity assessment — directly tests NMC FM8.7 and links to the Lillu 2013 Supreme Court ruling.
Tests understanding of legitimacy presumption and its medicolegal applications — a distinct legal concept from virginity that is relevant to inheritance and family law cases.
Tests application of signs of recent delivery to a forensic case of concealed delivery — a key competency for infanticide investigations.
Tests understanding of superfecundation — a rare but medicolegal-relevant phenomenon in disputed paternity cases.
Tests the key distinction between impotence and sterility — a terminological precision error that frequently appears in medicolegal reports and court testimony.
Applies medicolegal assessment principles for impotence to a civil case scenario — commonly encountered in nullity of marriage petitions.

Tests knowledge of who is permitted to commission surrogacy under the Surrogacy (Regulation) Act 2021 — a new Act with specific eligibility criteria that clinicians must know for medicolegal reporting.
Distinguishes the ART Act from the Surrogacy Act — two separate 2021 statutes that are often confused by students.
Applies PC&PNDT Act 1994 offence provisions to a clinical scenario — doctors must recognise what constitutes a violation to avoid criminal liability.
Tests understanding of the PWDVA 2005 as a civil remedy — commonly mischaracterised as a criminal statute, which changes the doctor's role in documentation.
Applies MTP Act 2021 amended gestational limits to a clinical scenario involving a rape victim — the most examined provision and most common examiner scenario.
Tests understanding of the docimasia pulmonum (hydrostatic test) and its limitations — directly relevant to infanticide post-mortem practice.
Tests differentiation of maceration (intrauterine death) signs from postmortem putrefaction — the most important distinction in infanticide autopsies affecting cause of death determination.

Tests understanding of SIDS as a natural diagnosis that must be excluded in infant death investigations before concluding homicide — prevents medicolegal error in the direction of both over-diagnosis and under-diagnosis of infanticide.
